about: Every NS…UsageDescription key in the evaluated Info.plist of Automatos Go (npx expo config --type introspect on the merged base 24a8fa6, 26 Oct 2026), as data (R07, KR12). kind 'used' is a permission the app asks for, with what it is for; kind 'notice' is a key Apple requires because a bundled library references the framework (ITMS-90683), although the app never asks. needs lists the framework classes that require the key, as docs/native-modules.md 'Symbols and usage keys' maps them (Framework: class); an empty needs carries a note. proposed is the privacy draft's Appendix A.3 string for the key (reports/mobile-review-2026-10-20/drafts/privacy-policy-automatos-go.md; null where A.3 proposes none), and differences lists, for Gerard, where the shipped string and the proposal differ. This story changes no shipped string: a change is an app.json edit, which moves the fingerprint and costs an iOS build. src/release/__tests__/permissions.test.ts holds the evaluated Info.plist to keys and strings here.

keys.string: Automatos Go uses the camera to scan the QR code that connects it to your server, and to take photos you send to Auto.
keys.proposed: Automatos Go uses the camera to scan the pairing code for your own server and to take photos you send to Auto.

keys.string: Automatos Go uses the microphone when you talk to Auto.
keys.proposed: Automatos Go uses the microphone while you hold to talk or are in an Auto Live call.

keys.string: Automatos Go turns what you say to Auto into text, using speech recognition on this iPhone.
keys.proposed: Automatos Go turns what you say into text on your iPhone, so you can talk to Auto.

keys.string: Automatos Go lets you choose photos from your library to attach to a message for Auto.
keys.proposed: Automatos Go opens your photo library only to attach the photos you pick.

keys.string: Automatos Go asks for Face ID before you approve a request or answer a question in your workspace.
keys.proposed: Automatos Go can check it's you before you approve or answer.

keys.string: Automatos Go connects to your own Automatos server when it runs on your home or office network.
keys.note: No class: iOS asks on the app's first connection to a device on the local network (the API client, for a self-hosted server on a private address).
keys.proposed: Automatos Go connects to your own Automatos server on this network.

keys.string: Automatos Go does not save anything to your photo library; a bundled library references it, so Apple requires this notice; the app never asks for access.
Automatos Go does not use motion data; a bundled library references it, so Apple requires this notice; the app never asks for access.

differences.difference: Same two purposes. Shipped says 'the QR code that connects it to your server'; A.3 says 'the pairing code for your own server'.
A.3 says when the microphone is open ('while you hold to talk or are in an Auto Live call'), which matches D33 (never in the background); shipped says only 'when you talk to Auto'.
Word order only: both say the speech becomes text on the iPhone, which the code holds to (quick-ask always starts with requiresOnDeviceRecognition true: src/voice/quick-ask/recognition-policy.ts).

A.3 adds 'only' and 'the photos you pick'; shipped names what they are for ('to attach to a message for Auto'). The library opens in the system photo picker (PHPicker), which gives the app only the photos chosen.
A.3's 'can check' says the check is optional, which it is (a setting: src/step-up/policy.ts); shipped's 'asks for Face ID before …' reads as always and names what is approved or answered.
Shipped says 'when it runs on your home or office network'; A.3 says 'on this network'.
A.3 proposes no string: it lists only the six keys the app uses. The shipped notice is the foundation's (US-002c).
